beats.role_note: The game, both effects, their jobs, and the event (A) and condition (B) that drive them (CHANGE-BRIEF A.1, B.1; main.gd).
beats.narration_text: The game: two tin toys box on wind-up springs, and every attack spends wind. Effect A is an impact burst. Its job, in Tharun's brief, is to give each hit distinct visual weight and better readability across backgrounds. Its event is every impact, a melee hit or a cork hit, both arriving at main's on impact, with a blocked flag. Effect B is wind steam at the fighter's back key, a feedback loop. Its condition is wind below twenty-five, and its mapping: amount ratio equals twenty-five minus wind, over twenty-five, clamped between zero and one.

beats.role_note: The three parts of a particle system, each with a scene-file line (impact_effect.tscn:86, 28, 37) and the visible result in the r1 strip; why the headless price is near zero (CLAUDE.md Headless facts).
beats.narration_text: Every particle system has three parts. Emission decides how many particles are born, and when. Line eighty-six, explosiveness one: all sixteen shards are born at once, and the burst is on screen in frame ten itself. Process moves each particle over its life. Line twenty-eight, gravity four hundred: the shards fall into a ring below the fist. Draw decides how each particle is painted. Line thirty-seven, blend mode one, which is add: the core can only brighten. In this game the process runs on the graphics card. A headless run uses a dummy renderer that runs no GPU particle process and draws nothing, so a GPU effect's headless price is near zero by construction.

beats.narration_text: Effect A's intent, written before the build. Timing: a quarter-second life, an instant snap expansion, then a smooth fade. Contrast: a dark edge and a bright core, on separate emitters, the shards in mix and the core in add. That split came from Claude Code's review: an additive layer cannot draw a dark outline. Scale: about sixty pixels wide in the window. Variation: random angle, speed and rotation, so rapid repeated hits never look stamped.

beats.narration_text: The first strip is a fixture: a preview scene with a fixed seed, a burst at frame ten and a second at frame eleven. Tharun looked first, before Claude read anything. The core flash, bright cyan, reads. The dark shards are a bit hard to make out. Claude's reading agreed and measured why: at frame fifteen the shards darken the castle by a median of only forty-one levels. The colour ramp fades alpha in a straight line, so two-thirds through life about a third is left. Frames twenty, thirty and fifty are empty, as the brief predicted.

beats.role_note: Effect A revision 1: the one-setting change (impact_effect.tscn:8-9, git 45e986f) and Claude's frame-by-frame prediction written before the change (TUNING.md).
beats.narration_text: Revision one changes one setting: the shards' colour ramp, lines eight and nine. A middle point at seven tenths keeps the charcoal fully opaque for most of the shard's life. Claude's prediction, written before any change: frame ten unchanged; frame twelve slightly darker; and at frame fifteen the median darkening rises from forty-one to ninety or more, with about the same count of dark pixels. The risk Claude named: the fade is squeezed into the last few frames, so the shards may blink out. Tharun approved the change.

beats.narration_text: r1, captured by Tharun with the same fixture and seed. Top row before, bottom row after. Frame fifteen: the median rose to one hundred and five point seven, so the median matches. The count does not: it rose by sixteen percent, because faint edge pixels now pass the threshold. Frame twelve: direction right, size wrong. Frame ten: almost; Claude had assumed the particles were zero frames old. The blink-out risk is something the strip cannot show, so it went to Tharun in the running game: they faded out smoothly, no snap or blink. His verdict: keep.

beats.role_note: The event wiring: main.gd:228-238 _spawn_impact (Claude, plan approved step by step by Tharun).
beats.narration_text: Now the event. Main's on impact keeps the star, the shake and the roll, then calls spawn impact. Line two twenty-nine picks the normal or the blocked scene from the blocked flag. Line two thirty-one makes the burst a child of Main at p, so a cork can free itself without taking the burst with it. And line two thirty-eight restarts each emitter after add child; the burst frees itself once both have finished. A fresh instance per hit, so rapid hits overlap instead of cutting each other off.

beats.narration_text: In play, from a scripted-input capture made for this film. Bolt taps jab each time he is ready, eight times; Rivet is the game's own brain. Every landed jab bursts. Every other jab, Rivet blocks, and that hit gets the smaller grey burst. Rivet's own hits on Bolt burst too. Again at quarter speed: each hit gets its own instance, and the counter shows how many are alive.

beats.role_note: Effect B intent: CHANGE-BRIEF B.1 (job, value, condition, mapping, feature A does not use) and B.2 (timing, scale), quoted verbatim.
beats.narration_text: Effect B is a feedback loop. Tharun's brief says players fighting at high speed cannot afford to look away from the sprites to check the dial, so the cue sits on the fighter's back, at the key. The value is wind, zero to one hundred. The condition: below twenty-five, the same threshold as the music's slowdown. The mapping: dormant at twenty-five and above, rising in a straight line to one at zero. And the feature Effect A doesn't use: amount ratio, which scales how many particles are emitted without restarting the system. Puffs should start around five pixels and grow to fifteen or twenty.

shot.note: Composite of real files, recorded output and real engine captures, built by _tools/make_media.py; labels name the provenance of every embedded image.

beats.role_note: Effect B as built: wind_steam.tscn:35-43 (node) beside main.gd:69-70 and 241-242 (attach, mapping).
beats.narration_text: The scene: one emitter. Amount twenty-five, the fixed maximum, and amount ratio zero: dormant. A life of six tenths of a second, and local coordinates on, so the puffs ride with the key. In main, line seventy: each time a fighter announces its wind, the steam's amount ratio is set from steam ratio. Lines two forty-one and two forty-two: twenty-five minus wind, over twenty-five, clamped. That is the only effect value any code sets.

beats.role_note: The first steam strip, captures/wind_steam/r0 (fixture), Tharun's first look, and Claude's later size measurement (TUNING.md, TEST-REPORT A6-5c).
beats.narration_text: The first steam strip, again a fixture: ratio one from frame ten, cut to zero at frame fifty. Frame forty is the steady plume; fifty-five, the tail fading; seventy, empty. Tharun's first look: fine white misty trails rising upward, and the entire steam rise is tall, roughly half of Bolt's height. Claude measured it afterwards at frame forty: eighteen by twenty-seven view pixels, about a quarter of Bolt's one hundred and twelve. That disagreement stands. We come back to it.

beats.role_note: Effect B revision 1: Tharun's in-game observation, the rewind strip r0 (fixture), the change (steam_mount.gd:31-35, Tharun's choice) and Claude's prediction (TUNING.md).
beats.narration_text: Revision one came from play. Tharun, in game: the steam cut out immediately upon triggering the rewind state. The first strip never rewinds, so Claude added a rewind fixture. Its strip, r0, frame thirty-four: the whole plume collapses to a thin sliver. The key spins, its x scale swings down to fifteen percent, and the steam, its child, squashes with it. Tharun chose the fix: a holder, Steam Mount, over turning local coordinates off. Lines thirty-three to thirty-five copy the key's position, facing and visibility, but not its squash. Claude's prediction: r1 equals r0 wherever the key was full width, and at frame thirty-four, a full-width plume.

beats.role_note: Rewind r0 vs r1 (captures/wind_steam_rewind/r0_vs_r1_sheet.png), Claude's comparison and Tharun's in-game verdict.
beats.narration_text: r1, same fixture, seed and flags. Top row before, bottom row after. Frames twenty-eight and thirty-one: zero pixels differ. Frame thirty-four: one thousand and twenty-one pixels differ, all in a small box above the key, a full soft plume where r0 had a sliver. Every later frame: zero. It matches. But the strip under-shows the old flicker: only one of seven rewind frames caught the key narrow. So the verdict was Tharun's, in game: it kept going and tapered off smoothly instead of cutting out. Keep.

beats.role_note: Effect B in play, start / pause / stop: the same Movie Maker capture (scripted input), with Bolt's wind, amount_ratio and pause read from the capture log each frame; state-test rows B-R1..B-R4.
beats.narration_text: In play, from the same scripted capture. After the seventh jab, Bolt's wind is sixteen: ratio point three six, and steam starts from the key. After the eighth, wind four: point eight four. Then pause. The fight freezes and the screen dims, but the steam keeps rising. It is the only thing that moves, because it inherits process mode always from Main. Play resumes, and Rivet lands a hit. Then rewind. Each click adds ten wind, the ratio steps down, point four four, point zero four, zero, and the puffs already alive fade out over their life instead of vanishing.

beats.role_note: Two annotated lines of the generated process shader (particles_generated.gdshader:258, 302 with 315) beside the brief settings they implement (B.3 spread 30.0, gravity (0, -180, 0)); Tharun's line references (TEST-REPORT "The process shader").
beats.narration_text: Under the hood. Tharun converted Effect B's process material in the editor and saved the shader Godot wrote; the game does not use this copy. Line two fifty-eight: each new puff gets a random direction from spread, times its starting speed. That spread is the brief's thirty degrees, a half-angle. Line three oh two: force starts as gravity, and line three fifteen adds force times delta to the velocity. That gravity is the brief's minus one eighty. The numbers themselves live on the material, so the shader only declares them as uniforms.

beats.role_note: What the tests proved: counts (logs/, re-run for this film on a clean copy of c844ab2) and the mutations (evidence/a6/mutations/, TEST-REPORT A6-1..A6-3).
beats.narration_text: What the tests proved, re-run for this film on a clean copy of c844ab2. The config tests read every brief value back from the scenes: one hundred thirty-six checks for Effect A and thirty-three for Effect B, none failed, including that spread of thirty and gravity of minus one eighty. The state tests drive real input: forty-four for A, thirty-seven for B. Then the mutations. A Godot three name: Godot loaded it with no warning, and the effect still fired, but one check failed. A value drift, sixteen shards to twelve: one failed. Never freeing a burst: five. Setting amount instead of amount ratio: eleven. And one did not fail: setting emitting before the burst entered the tree, because the predicted failure never happened.

beats.role_note: Both prices against the budget: headless wall-clock price (evidence/a6/cost/cost_effects_60fps.log), the GPU budgets (CHANGE-BRIEF F) and the effects-off reference (evidence/a6/visual-profiler-vulkan.webp, Tharun); the GPU price is not measured (TEST-REPORT A6-5: open).
beats.narration_text: And the price. The headless cost script includes an empty-scene control. The game without the effects costs about point zero two milliseconds a frame on the wall clock. Four bursts at once add point zero zero six, inside a spread of point zero one six. Full steam on both fighters: minus point zero zero zero seven. Neither can be told apart from the game without it, and two engine timers read zero throughout. The budgets are GPU budgets: Effect A under point five five milliseconds, Effect B under point two, against a point nine seven millisecond effects-off reference. The GPU price has not been measured yet. Those numbers are pending, and this film does not guess them. No headless run can show the look, or the GPU time.

beats.role_note: Agent mistakes caught (CHANGE-BRIEF A6 revisions, TEST-REPORT A6-2, A6-3, TUNING.md) and the readings of Claude's where Tharun's verdict differs (TEST-REPORT A6-5c, Tharun's statement verbatim).
beats.narration_text: Agent mistakes, caught. Claude cited main line two hundred for the cork's handler; it was one ninety-nine. Claude's first key list said R for rewind; it is S. Claude's first watch loop ran four times too fast. Claude's first state test compared two bursts after both were freed. And Claude's early probe was stated more broadly than the result supports. Where Tharun's verdict differs from Claude's readings: the shards looked bigger to him, though their scale is unchanged; and the steam looked like half of Bolt's height, against a measured quarter. In Tharun's words, he accepts the objective pixel measurements; however, he keeps his visual observation for gameplay evaluation. And once it went the other way: his first answer said the shards pop cleanly over the dark stretch, Claude measured forty-two against one hundred five, and he corrected it.

beats.narration_text: Who did what, as SOURCES dot m d records it. Tharun chose both effects and every value in the brief, drafting with Claude three point five Sonnet, and wrote every dated revision. He reviewed CLAUDE dot m d, took the Visual Profiler screenshot, ran every Movie Maker capture and both config mutations, approved each wiring step and tuning change, gave every first look and in-game verdict, and converted the process shader. Claude Code wrote the facts sheet and probes, built both effect scenes, the texture scripts, the tests, the fixtures, the wiring and Steam Mount, read and measured every strip, and drafted the docs. Both textures are written by code; there is no third-party art.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — checked by numbers / by eye, open (GPU price), uncertain, one next step; revision shown.
beats.narration_text: The verdict, at revision c eight four four a b two. Checked by numbers: every brief value read back, the rules in the state tests, five mutations caught, and one honestly not. Checked by eye: Tharun's first looks, both tuning verdicts, both backgrounds, scene load and the arena walls. Still open: the GPU price. Still uncertain: Effect A's shards lose most of their contrast over the dark stretch; Rivet rarely steams, because his brain rewinds at the same threshold; and whether a hidden emitter keeps simulating has not been checked. One next step: take the GPU price in the GPU price fixture, effect off against on at its heaviest, for each effect, against its budget.
